options.name: modbus
options.setting-help: the inverter Modbus settings

options.name: upstream
options.setting-help: the inverter Modbus endpoint
options.help: the inverter Modbus TCP endpoint HOST:PORT (`:5502` = 127.0.0.1:5502) (default: config, $UPSTREAM or 127.0.0.1:5502)

options.name: modbus-unit
options.setting-help: Modbus unit ID
options.help: Modbus unit id (default: config, $MODBUS_UNIT or 1)

options.name: modbus-offset
options.setting-help: added to register addresses
options.help: added to register addresses (default: config, $MODBUS_OFFSET or 0)

options.name: timeout
options.setting-help: Modbus connect/read timeout
options.help: Modbus timeout in seconds (default: config, $TIMEOUT or 3)

options.name: profile
options.setting-help: device profile JSON: the registers the metrics read (a bare name resolves in profiles/profiles/)
options.help: device profile JSON (the shared profiles/ schema; scrape-marked entries feed the metric registers) (default: config, $PROFILE or the bundled sun2000 profile)

options.name: metrics-spec
options.setting-help: metrics spec JSON, sectioned: {profile: {key: {help, profile?}}, compute: ..., scraper: ...} — merged in memory over the built-in lib/metrics.json scraper_* block
options.help: metrics spec JSON, sectioned: {profile: {key: {help, profile?}}, compute: ..., scraper: ...} — merged in memory over the built-in lib/metrics.json scraper_* block (default: config, $METRICS_SPEC or the bundled metrics.json)

options.name: metric-prefix
options.setting-help: the prefix on the profile- and compute-fed metric names
options.help: the prefix on the profile- and compute-fed metric names (default: config, $METRIC_PREFIX or 'huawei'); the bundled scraper_* names are fixed

options.name: max-kwp
options.setting-help: maximum PV array kWp
options.help: maximum PV array kWp (default: config, $MAX_KWP or 6; 0 = no checking)

options.name: max-grid-kw
options.setting-help: maximum grid kW, either direction
options.help: maximum grid kW, either direction (default: config, $MAX_GRID_KW or 12; 0 = no checking)

options.name: battery
options.setting-help: enable battery support
options.help: enable battery support (default: config, $BATTERY or off)

options.name: grid-positive-import
options.setting-help: grid register positive when importing
options.help: grid register positive when importing (default: config, $GRID_POSITIVE_IMPORT or positive = export)

options.name: listen
options.setting-help: listen address HOST:PORT
options.help: listen address HOST:PORT (default: config, $LISTEN or 127.0.0.1:9350)

options.name: local-time
options.setting-help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC
options.help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC

options.name: limits
options.setting-help: the HTTP serving limits (the client caps and the idle timeouts)

options.name: max-clients
options.setting-help: simultaneous HTTP clients on /metrics; extras get an immediate 503
options.help: maximum concurrent HTTP clients; extras get an immediate 503 (default: config, $MAX_CLIENTS or 64; 0 = unlimited)

options.name: client-timeout
options.setting-help: kick idle keep-alive HTTP clients after this long

value-help.0: never (the built-in slowloris cap still applies on the metrics surfaces that have one)

options.help: seconds an idle keep-alive HTTP client is kept before being kicked (default: config, $CLIENT_TIMEOUT or 300; 0 = off)

options.name: max-conn-per-ip
options.setting-help: simultaneous HTTP connections from one peer IP
options.help: maximum concurrent HTTP connections from one peer IP; extras get an immediate 503 (default: config, $MAX_CONN_PER_IP or 0 = no per-IP limit)

options.name: control
options.setting-help: the control plane: the tokens, the ops role's RBAC policy, the trusted peers

options.name: control-port
options.setting-help: JSON-lines control server target: unix socket path
options.help: JSON-lines control server target: unix socket path (default: /tmp/modbus-scraper-<listen-port>.socket) or TCP port number on 127.0.0.1 (e.g. 15599); 0 = off. Talk to it with modbus-scraper-ctl.py (default: config, $CTL)

options.name: control-token
options.setting-help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token": ...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token
options.help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token": ...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token (default: config, $CONTROL_TOKEN or none)

options.name: control-token-file
options.setting-help: the control token from a file (the first line; e.g. a systemd LoadCredential or a key file; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-token; giving both is an error (env CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE)
options.help: the control token from a file (the first line; e.g. a systemd LoadCredential or a key file; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-token; giving both is an error (env CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE)

options.name: control-ops-token
options.setting-help: a second, read-only control token: sessions authenticating with it may run the show/clear verbs only (no set/unset, no poll now, no request reload, no restart, no shutdown) — the ops shift against the admin key, both audited
options.help: a second, read-only control token: sessions authenticating with it may run the show/clear verbs only (no set/unset, no poll now, no request reload, no restart, no shutdown) — the ops shift against the admin key, both audited (default: config, $CONTROL_OPS_TOKEN or none)

options.name: control-ops-token-file
options.setting-help: the read-only ops token from a file (the first line; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-ops-token; giving both is an error
options.help: the read-only ops token from a file (the first line; must be owner-only 0600) — takes the place of --control-ops-token; giving both is an error (default: config, $CONTROL_OPS_TOKEN_FILE)

options.name: control-ops-verbs
options.setting-help: the read-only ops role's RBAC policy: the verbs its sessions may run, comma-separated
options.help: the read-only ops role's RBAC policy: the verbs its sessions may run, comma-separated (default: show,clear; validated against the control grammar at start)

options.name: control-trust-uids
options.setting-help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted
options.help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted (default: config, $CONTROL_TRUST_UIDS or none)

options.name: auth-token
options.setting-help: require Authorization: Bearer <token> on all requests — rotates live; the value never renders back
options.help: require Authorization: Bearer <token> on all requests (default: config, $AUTH_TOKEN or disabled)

options.name: auth-token-file
options.setting-help: read the bearer token from this file instead (single line, trimmed; re-read on every SIGHUP — rotate by rewriting the file and reloading; must be owner-only 0600); mutually exclusive with --auth-token
options.help: read the bearer token from this file instead (single line, trimmed; re-read on every SIGHUP — rotate by rewriting the file and reloading; must be owner-only 0600); mutually exclusive with --auth-token

options.name: audit-log
options.setting-help: SCR audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); default: the XDG state home (~/.local/state/modbus-scraper/audit.log)
options.help: SCR audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); default: the XDG state home (~/.local/state/modbus-scraper/audit.log)

options.name: audit-max-mb
options.setting-help: rotate the audit log at this size in MB, keeping 3 backups; 0 = no size rotation (default %(default)s)
options.help: rotate the audit log at this size in MB, keeping 3 backups; 0 = no size rotation (default %(default)s)

options.name: audit-files
options.setting-help: rotated audit backups to keep (default %(default)s)
options.help: rotated audit backups to keep (default %(default)s)

options.name: no-audit-log
options.setting-help: disable the SCR audit trail
options.help: disable the SCR audit trail

options.name: interval
options.setting-help: seconds between polls of the inverter
options.help: seconds between polls (default: config, $INTERVAL or 10)

options.name: log-access
options.setting-help: log every HTTP request at INFO

value-help.on: audit trail for who polled /metrics and when

options.help: log every HTTP request at INFO (default: config, $LOG_ACCESS or quiet)

options.name: log-level
options.setting-help: log verbosity

value-help.DEBUG: per-poll detail + the HTTP access log at DEBUG

options.help: log level (default: config, $LOG_LEVEL or INFO)

options.name: dump
options.setting-help: the state dump: the live overrides' file, the restore-on-start

options.name: dump-path
options.setting-help: the state dump file: the live overrides, written on request dump and the graceful shutdown
options.help: the state dump: the live setting overrides (the poll plan, the caps, the log surface — the tokens apart) as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on the request dump command and the graceful shutdown; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command (default: config, $DUMP_PATH or none)

options.name: dump-key
options.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the reload's state file too)
options.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the state rides encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash (default: config, $DUMP_KEY or none)

options.name: restore-on-start
options.setting-help: the dump loads on start (off: on demand with request restore)
options.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — the live overrides ride again instead of a cold start; default: start cold, load only on demand (default: config, $RESTORE_ON_START)

show.name: status
show.setting-help: multi-line effective state report: one key=value per field

show.name: connections
show.setting-help: the live HTTP clients of /metrics: the gate counters, one row per peer IP

show.name: config
show.setting-help: the effective configuration as a set-grammar script (the secret knobs render as *** SECRET REMOVED ***)

show.name: knobs
show.setting-help: the dictionary of all knobs: every knob, its flag, its env twin, its section, how it changes

commands.name: set
commands.help: configure a setting (set interval 5, set log-access on)

commands.name: unset
commands.help: restore a setting to its configured value (unset interval, unset log-level)

commands.name: inspect
commands.help: one pretty dump of everything (the state, the counters, the caps)

commands.name: show
commands.help: print a setting, the status report, or all of them

commands.name: request
commands.help: request reload re-reads the config (the SIGHUP path); with a dump path: request dump / request restore

commands.name: reload
commands.help: save the live overrides and restart the whole daemon (the config file and the flags are re-resolved)

commands.name: restart
commands.help: drop the Modbus session (reconnects on the next poll)
